transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-16 08:30 PT / 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Leo Martinez (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Head of ML, IvyBridge), Grace Liu (CTO), Omar Hassan (Infra)

Summary: 
Quick discovery focused on budget guardrails: per-token budget ceilings, how batching and KV/prefix cache move the needle, and whether IvyBridge should start on Hosted or go straight to Dedicated/Private given compliance and cost ops. Customer wants a short pilot to validate cost and latency with 3 model families.

Topics: budgeting, batching, caching, hosted vs dedicated vs vpc/private, SOC2/KMS, pilot scope, timeline, stakeholders

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference and with me is Leo our solutions engineer. um so first can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Ravi: yeah sure I'm Ravi, head of ML at IvyBridge, we run prod recommender and a new summarization feature, been looking at inference costs.
[00:18] Grace: Grace here, CTO, tagging in on procurement and security; Omar's infra.
[00:23] Omar: hey all.
[00:25] Leo: great, thanks. objective for today is to map your budget guardrails and the tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private. we'll also propose a lean pilot.
[00:36] Ravi: sound good. real quick, current stack: we use an internal microservice calling OpenAI for gen, but we have a 10k per month token cap on costs, and it's getting eaten. latency is okay now but cost spikes when usage bursts, and we need predictable unit econ.
[00:51] Grace: also compliance - we do have customer data in prompts sometimes; need to understand residency and KMS options. SOC-2 is a must for vendor.
[01:02] Maya: perfect, noted. couple clarifying Qs: 1) what are your SLA expectations — p99 latency target? 2) what's the monthly token budget and can it be reallocated? 3) who will sign the SOW, procurement timeline?
[01:18] Ravi: p99 target about 400-500ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), but for longer summarization we can tolerate up to 1.2s. token budget is approx $12k a month right now but we expect growth. procurement timeline is Q3 for pilot approval.
[01:33] Omar: infra note — we prefer VPC/private for model keys, but can do hosted if keys live with Redwood KMS integration, not sure yet.
[01:44] Leo: okay good. so the big levers we'll discuss: per-token pricing differences, batching and concurrency (tradeoff with tail latency), and KV/prefix caching which reduces repeat token generation. we also look at quantization / model family choices (small vs medium).
[01:58] Grace: can you put rough numbers on how much batching helps? we saw slide decks from other vendors but they're fuzzy.
[02:06] Maya: yes, we'll send a worked example. rough rule: batching increases throughput and reduces per-token cost, but raises p99. continuous batching strategies and dynamic batch size can keep p99 within your target while saving 15-40% per token in typical workloads.
[02:22] Ravi: 15-40% big range. how much of that is dependent on request size distribution? our traffic is a mix: 60% short chat-like, 40% summarization with longer contexts.
[02:34] Leo: exactly. if short chat dominates, batching can be aggressive; for mixed workloads we do workload-aware batching and prefix cache. for example, if you have repeated prefixes across requests — like user metadata or system prompts — prefix/KV cache can eliminate model recomputation for the prefix and save 20-60% on tokens depending on hit rate. we call it KV but some transcripts mention 'kay-vee' cache, ha.
[02:58] Grace: okay, and how does that interact with Dedicated? is it different vs hosted?
[03:04] Leo: under Dedicated you get reserved GPUs so throughput is predictable and you can tune batching aggressively because you control concurrency limits; Hosted has multi-tenant routing but Redwood offers dedicated routing pools and guaranteed capacity tiers. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you the most control but adds ops overhead and usually a higher fixed platform fee.
[03:22] Ravi: curious about unit-econ math. what inputs do you need to model our per-token cost if we run a pilot?
[03:29] Maya: we need your traffic profile (tokens per request distribution), target p99, desired availability, and whether caching can be enabled for X% of requests. from that we simulate throughput and compute per-token cost across hosted vs dedicated vs private with assumed GPU instance prices.
[03:42] Omar: do you account for KV cache memory pressure? our infra team worries about keeping large KV caches in memory on GPU and cost of DRAM.
[03:50] Leo: yes we model cache footprint and eviction. Redwood runtime supports off-GPU KV with fast retrieval in many cases and prefix-only caching for very high hit-rate use cases. that changes the cost tradeoff because you pay a bit more for memory but save on compute tokens.
[04:05] Grace: security — can you summarize options for encryption and key management?
[04:10] Maya: hosted supports customer-managed keys via supported KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) on certain plans; Dedicated and Private support HSM integrations and full bring-your-own-key. We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation docs we can share — link to security pack in notes.
[04:26] Ravi: great. thought exercise: if we cap at $12k/month, what are the knobs to stay under that while enabling growth to Q3?
[04:35] Leo: knobs: 1) model selection — move from large to medium or quantized variants for non-critical flows; 2) caching — enable prefix/KV cache for repeat prompts; 3) dynamic routing — send latency-sensitive requests to higher-cost low-latency pool and bulk async to cheaper pools; 4) token-slicing — truncate or reformulate prompts. With these we can often reduce per-token cost 30% without big UX regressions.
[04:58] Maya: and we can set hard budget guardrails on routes so if spend hits threshold traffic routes can degrade gracefully or fallback to cheaper models.
[05:07] Grace: do you have an example of a guardrail policy?
[05:11] Leo: yes: e.g., route A (front-facing chat) has p99 <= 450ms, budget share 60% of tokens; route B (summarizer) is cost-priority with async batching, budget share 40%. On hitting monthly budget 90% we can throttle lower-priority routes or switch them to a quantized model.
[05:28] Ravi: sounds practical. pilot — what would you propose as minimal bench to validate unit econ?
[05:33] Maya: lean pilot: 1 week of replayed traffic (or synthetic mix) over 3 model variants (large, quantized-large, medium), with caching on/off and batching configs. Collect p50/p95/p99 + cost per 1k tokens. Leo will draft the test matrix.
[05:48] Omar: who runs the pilot — Redwood hosted or our infra? we prefer Redwood to run initial bench in hosted to avoid ops lift.
[05:55] Leo: we can run in Redwood hosted with dedicated capacity for the pilot or spin up a lightweight private env depending on security caveats. for data residency you can obfuscate prompts and run with synthetic or hashed tokens.
[06:06] Grace: procurement — we'll need pricing sheet + SOW to route to procurement. can you provide seat/license style for Dedicated?
[06:14] Maya: yes, we'll include hosted per-token price tiers, dedicated reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit tiers), and private deployment licensing in the sheet. we'll also include sample SOW language.
[06:24] Ravi: any hard surprises on the cost model? hidden fees?
[06:27] Maya: main components are platform fee for dedicated/private, compute cost (GPU amortized), and usage (per-token). There can be egress/network costs for private deployments depending on your cloud. we'll call those out.
[06:38] Leo: also note that when you do higher batching to save costs you may need more episodes of tail latency tuning; we can help with benchmark tuning.
[06:47] Grace: how do rollouts work? if a model regresses how do you fallback?
[06:51] Leo: Redwood supports route-level rollouts, canary percentages, and automatic fallback to a cheaper or safer model variant on quality/regression. plus per-prompt eval hooks.
[07:03] Ravi: ok, question on caching: what hit rate do you typically assume to see 20% savings?
[07:09] Leo: depends on app, but for prompt-heavy recommender flows 10-30% hit is realistic off the bat, with engineering changes to increase hit to 40-60% (prompt normalization, user-id hashing).
[07:21] Grace: do you provide observability for token spend per route and per model?
[07:25] Maya: yes full token-level and route-level breakdowns in Redwood Console; we can export CSVs into your internal chargeback system.
[07:33] Omar: about SLA and sustained bursts — if we exceed reserved capacity can you burst?
[07:38] Leo: yes Dedicated supports burst capacity options. Hosted has cross-tenant fallback policies to similar model variants; you can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper model to keep requests served.
[07:49] Ravi: I'd like a worked example now — say we run 2m tokens/day, avg token length 120, 60% short chat, 40% long summarize; what's the hosted per-token ballpark?
[07:59] Maya: we didn't have your exact model choices; but conservative hosted ballpark for a medium LLM might be $0.0008 - 0.0015 per token before batching. With batching and caching that could drop to $0.0005 - 0.001. For dedicated, if you commit to a month of capacity, effective per-token could be 20-50% lower depending on utilization.
[08:20] Grace: that's helpful. procurement will push for committed pricing if we can hit utilization.
[08:26] Leo: yes we can show utilization scenarios.
[08:28] Maya: ok loop back to actions: we'll send unit-econ model and propose pilot plan. any other blockers?
[08:34] Grace: please share SOC2 and KMS details.
[08:36] Ravi: and the benchmark plan.
[08:38] Omar: also include expected memory footprint for KV cache options in the pilot doc.
[08:42] Maya: noted. I'll include links: security pack (https://redwood.ai/security/ivybridge-pack) and pilot deck (https://redwood.ai/sales/decks/ivybridge-budget-deck).
[08:52] Grace: perfect.
[08:54] Maya: cool thanks everyone we'll follow up by Friday with docs and the test matrix.
[08:59] Ravi: thanks.
[09:00] (meeting ends)

Recap / Close:
- Pilot agreed: 1 week replay/bench on hosted with dedicated test pool; 3 model variants; caching on/off; measure cost and p99.
- Redwood to share pricing sheet, unit-econ workbook, security pack, and pilot test matrix.
- Customer to confirm procurement window and security lead.
